title: Granite
description: Light gray medium-coarse-grained quartz-plagioclase-muscovite granite

title: Northfield Formation
description: Silvery dark gray to black phyllites and slates with 1-2 mm pyrites visible on foliation planes, locally interlayered with massive brown calcareous dirty marble layers and gray quartzite layers

title: Shaw Mountain Formation
description: Cream colored, soft, thinly foliated meta-limestones interlayered with gray phyllites

title: Cram Hill Formation
description: Rusty-weathering, silvery gray to black, pyritiferous and often graphitic phyllites and phyllitic granofels greywackes. Massive weakly-foliated, granular metadiabasic dikes and sills of the Mt. Norris Intrusive Suite (MNIS) (Kim et al., 2003) occur locally; these intrusions have chilled margins and plagioclase phenocrysts

title: Cram Hill Formation
description: Green calcareous greenstone (metavolcanic) that becomes more massive and granular along-strike to the north

title: Cram Hill Formation
description: Rusty-weathering, light gray, sulfidic, fine-grained, flinty granofels/ metasiltone

title: Cram Hill Formation
description: Same as Ocr, but has numerous horizons of massive dark gray phyllitic amphibolite

title: Cram Hill Formation
description: Interlayered light green granofels and grayish-green phyllites

title: Moretown Formation, Bayley-Hazen Member
description: Soft, thinly foliated, grayish-green phyllite with conspicuous layers of rusty weathering, pearly white granofels. Interlayered with Umbrella Hill Conglomerate (CObh1)

title: Moretown Formation, Bayley-Hazen Member
description: Rusty-weathering dark gray to black graphitic phyllite. Interlayered with Umbrella Hill Conglomerate (CObh1)

title: Moretown Formation, Bayley-Hazen Member, Umbrella Hill Conglomerate
description: Silvery-gray phyllitic conglomerate composed of pebbles and cobbles of coarsely-crystalline vein quartz, pink to red slate, tan granofels, black phyllite, and amphibolite. Unoriented chlorotoid found in pelitic clasts and phyllitic matrix. Top of this unit (east) is interlayered with COmbh2 and COmbh3

title: Moretown Formation, Western Member
description: Light gray fine-grained granofels metasiltstone, gray and tan quartzites, gray and black slates, with massive, gray, granular metadiabasic dikes of the Mt. Norris Intrusive Suite (MNIS)(Kim et al., 2003); these intrusions have chilled margins and plagioclase phenocrysts

title: Moretown Formation, Wild Branch Member
description: Grayish-green phyllites interlayered with massive light green quartzo-feldspathic phyllitic granofels; spaced cleavage gives the granofels a pinstriped appearance; greenstones are common and may have compositions intermediate between greenstone and feldspathic phyllitic granofels. Massive, gray, granular, metadiabasic dikes of the Mt. Norris Intrusive Suite (MNIS) (Kim et al., 2003)occur locally; these dikes and sills have chilled margins and plagioclase phenocrysts

title: Moretown Formation, Wild Branch Member
description: Massive well foliated greenstone

title: Moretown Formation, Wild Branch Member
description: Rusty-weathering dark gray to black graphitic phyllite

title: Ottauquechee Formation
description: Rusty-weathering gray to black phyllite that is usually graphitic and pyritiferous; isoclinally folded and transposed quartz veins are abundant

title: Ottauquechee Formation
description: Massive well foliated greenstone with abnormally high quartz content; may have a volcaniclastic origin

title: Ottauquechee Formation
description: Silvery grayish green phyllitic meta-greywacke with conspicuous smoky gray sub-rounded quartz pebbles; frequently rusty-weathering and interlayered with grayish green and black phyllites

title: Ultramafic rocks
description: Massive serpentinized ultramafic; margins may consist of strongly foliated talc carbonate or "blackwall" which is composed of chlorite, serpentine, and magnetite

title: Stowe Formation
description: Grayish-green phyllites with abundant isoclinally folded and transposed quartz veins; massive, gray, granular meta-diabasic dikes and sills of the Mt. Norris Intrusive Suite (MNIS) (Kim et al., 2003) occur throughout; these intrusions have chilled margins and plagioclase phenocrysts

title: Stowe Formation
description: Rusty-weathering gray to black phyllite that is usually graphitic and pyritiferous; isoclinally folded and transposed quartz veins are abundant

title: Stowe Formation
description: Massive well foliated bodies of dark green greenstone; rusty Fe carbonate splotches often give this unit a punky appearance; locally interlayered with grayish-green or black phyllites

title: Stowe Formation
description: Grayish-green phyllites that are interlayered with rusty-weathering black phyllites; this interlayering can occur within a single outcrop or within a series of closely spaced outcrops and is too fine to portray on this map; isoclinally folded and transposed quartz veins are abundant; thin greenstones occur locally

title: Stowe Formation
description: Same as CZslm1 except for the presence of massive, gray, granular metadiabasic dikes and sills of the Mt. Norris Intrusive Suite (MNIS)(Kim et al. 2003); these intrusions have chilled margins and plagioclase phenocrysts

title: Stowe Formation
description: Tan-weathering gray phyllitic granofels that have a granular appearance due to the high quartz content

title: Hazens Notch Formation
description: Silvery grayish-green albite porphyroblast schist interlayered with thin greenstones along the Burgess Branch Fault Zone

title: Hazens Notch Formation
description: Rusty-weathering, gray to black, graphitic and pyritiferous schist with white and black albite porphyroblasts; locally interlayered with gray and black laminated quartzites
